type:
∀ φ : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Part _root_.Nat,
  _root_.AcceptableNumbering φ →
  ∀ stage : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Finset _root_.Nat,
    _root_.Computable (fun p : _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat × _root_.Nat =>
      (_root_.Equiv.symm _root_.Finset.equivBitIndices)
        (stage p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)) →
    (∀ e x : _root_.Nat, _root_.Monotone (stage e x)) →
    let V : _root_.Nat → _root_.Nat → _root_.Set _root_.Nat :=
      fun e x => {y | ∃ s : _root_.Nat, y ∈ stage e x s}
    (∀ i : _root_.Nat, ∃ e : _root_.Nat, ∀ x y : _root_.Nat,
      y ∈ V e x ↔ _root_.Part.Dom (φ i (_root_.Nat.pair x y))) →
    let K : _root_.Set _root_.Nat := {n |
      let (i, z) := _root_.Nat.unpair n
      _root_.Part.Dom (φ i z)}
    (_root_.RelativeComputabilityAndEnumerability K).1 {n |
      let (e, p) := _root_.Nat.unpair n
      let (x, t) := _root_.Nat.unpair p
      ∀ r : _root_.Nat, t ≤ r → stage e x r = stage e x t}
sourceReason: The endpoint is the fixed-stage oracle decision in the upper-requirement strategy of §4, p. 8, of arXiv:2609.00419v1. The stage sets are finite and increase to their row unions. The exhaustion hypothesis represents the enumeration of all uniformly c.e. families by their paired domains. Stage outputs use binary finite-set codes. The decision takes Nat.pair e (Nat.pair x t) as input and uses the paired halting set of the acceptable numbering as the oracle. The article-specific portal and defect report both returned HTTP 404, so no correction could be verified. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00419v1#page=8 https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419 https://alphabetamath.cc/research-portal/nonrecursive-many-one-degrees-2609-00419/prerequisite-omissions-and-potential-defects
